sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Define communication.
questions.answer: A process of interaction in which information, ideas and attitudes are transmitted between people to bring about a change in behaviour.

questions.q: Name the two types of communication.
Name the four channels of non-verbal communication.
State true or false: (i) We cannot communicate through gestures. (ii) The majority of our communication is non-verbal.
State true or false: (i) People have unlimited capacity to process information. (ii) Effective communication can be achieved by talking fast.
Name any two barriers to effective communication.
questions.answer: Information overload, selective perception, emotions, differing word meanings (any two).

questions.q: Name any two features of effective communication.
questions.answer: Common frame of reference, mutual interest, common language, common environment (any two).

questions.q: Give any two positive influences of media.
questions.answer: Educates and improves academic performance; promotes health awareness; informs about government policy (any two).

questions.q: Fill in: Reading, speaking, writing or listening are examples of ______ communication; touch as a channel is called ______.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Identify the channel: (i) body movement; (ii) eye contact; (iii) social distance; (iv) touch.
Give the distance zones: (i) intimate; (ii) personal; (iii) social; (iv) public.
questions.answer: (i) 0–18 inches. (ii) 18 inches–4 feet. (iii) 4–12 feet. (iv) beyond 12 feet.

questions.q: What is indicated by (i) direct eye contact; (ii) downward look; (iii) one raised eyebrow; (iv) both eyebrows raised?
questions.answer: (i) Confidence. (ii) Respect, careful listening or guilt. (iii) Doubt. (iv) Admiration.

questions.q: Give the five elements of communication (any four).
questions.answer: Two-way process, message, commonness of understanding, modifying behaviour, method of giving information.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is meant by commonness of understanding?
questions.answer: Sender and receiver share a base such as culture, language and environment, making words, idioms and gestures meaningful to both.

questions.q: Why is non-verbal communication important?
questions.answer: It makes up most of communication, reinforces words, expresses emotions and attitudes and regulates interaction.

questions.q: What is proxemics?
questions.answer: The use of social distance between people: intimate, personal, social and public space.

questions.q: What is information overload?
questions.answer: A situation in which too much information exceeds a person's limited capacity, so some is ignored or forgotten.

questions.q: Why is a common environment important in communication?
questions.answer: People from similar backgrounds such as nationality, class, culture or profession understand each other easily.

questions.q: What is propaganda?
questions.answer: An organised way of spreading false or biased information.

questions.q: Explain 'high power-distance index' in India.
questions.answer: Hierarchy, authority and age strongly shape communication, distance and eye contact between superiors and subordinates.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the key elements of communication.
questions.answer: Two-way sender–receiver process, a message, commonness of understanding, modification of the receiver's behaviour and a method of giving information (words or gestures).

questions.q: Describe the functions of non-verbal communication.
questions.answer: It creates impressions beyond words, reinforces speech, expresses emotions and attitudes, conveys power, affection, respect, regulates interaction and allows self-presentation; it is culture-bound.

questions.q: Describe the barriers to effective communication.
questions.answer: Distortion of facts to please others, selective perception, projection in decoding, information overload, emotional states and differing meanings of words by age, gender and culture.

questions.q: Describe the features of effective communication.
questions.answer: Common frame of reference, mutual interest, common language and common environment ensure minimum misunderstanding.

questions.q: Give tips for improving verbal and body language.
questions.answer: Read and listen to improve language, modulate voice, think before speaking, avoid speaking fast or loudly; keep appropriate distance, touch only if needed, keep eye contact in interviews and look confident.

questions.q: Describe the negative impacts of media.
questions.answer: Spread of wrong news, rumours and propaganda leading to violence and prejudice, invasion of privacy, vulgar material and unhealthy influence on children's body image and lifestyle.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Define communication and discuss its five elements with examples.
questions.answer: Communication is interaction to transmit information and bring behaviour change. Elements: two-way process (teacher to students), message (idea or feeling), commonness of understanding (language, culture), behaviour change (running out when told of a fire) and a method (words or gestures).

questions.q: Discuss verbal and non-verbal communication and their importance.
questions.answer: Verbal uses spoken or written words (10–11 hours daily). Non-verbal (more than 70 per cent) uses kinesics, gaze, proxemics (four distance zones) and haptics; eye contact, posture and smile convey meaning. It supports words, expresses emotion, regulates interaction and varies with culture.

questions.q: Explain the barriers and the features of effective communication.
questions.answer: Barriers: distortion, selective perception, projection, overload, emotions and differing word meanings. Effective communication needs a common frame of reference, mutual interest, common language and common environment, plus tips: voice modulation, thinking before speaking, appropriate distance and culturally sensitive signs.

questions.q: Discuss non-verbal communication in the Indian context and the role of media.
questions.answer: In India no public intimacy between couples, bangle gesture, handshakes mainly same-sex, a high power-distance (downcast eyes before superiors, veils, touching feet), personal space of 1.5–2 metres. Media informs, educates and integrates but can spread rumours, hatred and obscenity; it must follow ethics and promote national integration.
